hyperedges.label: Engineer Tester and Reviewer Delivery Roles

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.rationale: Registration normalizes email before uniqueness checks and stores password hashes, never plaintext. Login issues a 15-minute JWT and a 7-day refresh token stored as a hash. Refresh rotates the token. Reuse of a rotated token revokes the token family and forces login again so a stolen already-rotated token cannot keep a parallel session. Logout revokes the current refresh session.

nodes.label: Full-Text Search
nodes.rationale: Search uses PostgreSQL full-text search over the title and readable text extracted from TipTap. Formatting metadata and internal JSON attributes are not searchable, so hits match what a reader sees. Deleted notes are excluded, ownership is enforced, and results paginate in a stable order with highlights where the query supports them. The index updates on create, edit, restore, and delete.

nodes.label: Note
nodes.rationale: An authenticated user creates, reads, and updates their own notes. Creating a note and its initial version snapshot is atomic. Invalid or oversized updates must not change the note or create a snapshot. Autosave failure keeps the local draft and offers retry, and the UI shows saving, saved, and failed states.

nodes.label: OTP Password Reset
nodes.rationale: Real email delivery is out of scope, so the OTP is logged to the server console in development. Responses avoid revealing whether an email is registered. Baseline is 10-minute expiry, at most 5 attempts, and a 60-second resend cooldown. Resend invalidates the previous OTP. A successful reset consumes the OTP and requires a new password that meets policy. Rate limits apply per account and per IP.

nodes.label: Ownership
nodes.rationale: Notes are single-user-owned. Authenticated endpoints verify the access token and enforce ownership, so one account cannot read, update, list, search, or restore another account's notes. Real-time collaboration, attachments, native mobile apps, OAuth, nested folders, and real email delivery are out of scope.

nodes.label: Note List Pagination
nodes.rationale: Owners list their own non-deleted notes with pagination, sorting, and tag filters. Default page size is 20 and the maximum is 100. Stable order is updatedAt descending, then id, so tied timestamps do not skip or duplicate rows across pages. Trash is excluded unless the trash view is requested. Another user's notes never appear.

nodes.label: Public Visitor
nodes.rationale: May view a note only through a valid public share link. Cannot edit, see history, manage tags, or open the owner's other notes.

nodes.label: Registered User
nodes.rationale: May manage only their own notes, tags, authentication session, share links, and note history.

nodes.label: Share Link
nodes.rationale: Owners create a public read-only link with a cryptographically unpredictable token. Default expiry is 7 days, the maximum is 30 days, and non-expiring links are unsupported so a leaked link dies. Expired, revoked, invalid, or deleted-note links expose nothing. The public payload omits history and private owner metadata. View counts are an approximate metric: count a view after a successful page load, dedupe the same anonymous browser for 30 minutes, and skip obvious automation.

nodes.label: System Maintenance Role
nodes.rationale: Performs token validation, rate limiting, expiry enforcement, and scheduled cleanup of expired records so those controls do not depend on a user request.

nodes.label: Tag
nodes.rationale: Tags are user-scoped, trimmed, and unique within the owner's namespace. Deleting a tag removes associations and does not delete notes. Counts include the applicable non-deleted notes and must match between UI and API. Multi-tag filters use AND semantics so a note must have every selected tag. Clearing the selection removes the filter.

nodes.label: TipTap JSON Content
nodes.rationale: Canonical content is structured TipTap JSON, not HTML, limited to approved nodes, marks, attributes, and nesting. The server is authoritative so client checks are only immediate feedback, and content is never silently truncated. An empty valid document is allowed. Limits are 200 Unicode code points for a trimmed title, 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes, depth 20 with the root at zero, and 10,000 nodes.

nodes.label: Trash
nodes.rationale: Delete sets deletedAt and hides the note from ordinary lists and search. The owner can restore within 30 days, which clears deletedAt. Physical deletion during that window is forbidden so recovery stays possible. After 30 days a scheduled cleanup permanently purges the note, its versions, and its share links, and recovery is then unavailable.

nodes.label: Version History
nodes.rationale: Each qualifying save snapshots title and canonical content, including the initial create. Identical consecutive snapshots are deduplicated so history is not noise. Restore writes the chosen title and content back onto the note and records a new version, so a restore can be audited and reversed. Restored content must pass current validation. Restore is atomic. History stays private to the owner and is unavailable on share links.

nodes.label: Note
nodes.rationale: Stores id, owner id, title, TipTap JSON, search data, timestamps, and deletedAt. Search data lives on the note so full-text indexing can follow create, edit, restore, and delete without a second content store.

nodes.label: NoteTag
nodes.rationale: Associates a note and a tag with a unique pair constraint so the same tag cannot be attached twice and tag filters can join through one table.

nodes.label: NoteVersion
nodes.rationale: Stores the note id, a title snapshot, a TipTap JSON snapshot, and a creation timestamp. Snapshots are separate rows so history can outlive later edits of the current note.

nodes.label: Note Version Transactions
nodes.rationale: Create-plus-initial-snapshot, update-plus-snapshot, and version restore run in transactions so a failure cannot leave a note without its history or history without the note.

nodes.label: PasswordResetChallenge
nodes.rationale: Stores a user or email reference, a protected OTP, expiry, attempts, and consumption or resend data. The OTP is protected rather than stored as plaintext so a database read is not itself a reset credential.

nodes.label: RefreshTokenSession
nodes.rationale: Stores the user id, token hash, token-family or session id, expiry, and revocation timestamps. Hashing means a database read cannot replay a refresh token. Family tracking is what makes reuse detection revoke every session in that chain.

nodes.label: Scheduled Cleanup
nodes.rationale: An idempotent job removes expired authentication records and, after the 30-day recovery window, purges notes, versions, and share links. Idempotence lets the job run twice safely. Soft delete via deletedAt forbids physical deletion inside the window. Private operations authenticate and enforce ownership on the server. Passwords, refresh tokens, OTP secrets, and share-token secrets are never logged. Rate limits cover authentication, OTP, refresh, search, and sensitive writes.

nodes.label: ShareLink
nodes.rationale: Stores the note id, a secure token lookup or hash, expiry, revocation, and view-count data. The raw token is not the lookup key, so a database leak does not publish every live link.

nodes.label: Tag
nodes.rationale: Stores id, owner id, and name plus normalization fields. Uniqueness is per owner so two users can reuse the same visible tag name.

nodes.label: Ticket Sequence
nodes.rationale: Approved order is AB-1001 project setup, AB-1002 authentication, AB-1003 OTP password reset, AB-1004 note CRUD and soft delete, AB-1005 pagination sorting and tag filters, then AB-1006 tags and counts, AB-1007 search, AB-1008 sharing, AB-1009 version history, AB-1010 authentication UI, AB-1011 notes list UI, AB-1012 TipTap editor and autosave, AB-1013 search UI, AB-1014 share modal, AB-1015 history drawer and restore, and AB-1016 Playwright journey. Ticket ids and scope stay as approved.

nodes.label: User
nodes.rationale: Stores id, email, normalized email, password hash, and timestamps. Normalized email is unique so registration identity does not depend on casing or surrounding whitespace.

nodes.label: Email Normalization
nodes.rationale: Recommended policy, pending the approved rule: trim surrounding whitespace and lowercase for identity and uniqueness. Dots and plus aliases are kept so those addresses remain distinct users.

nodes.label: JWT Access Token
nodes.rationale: Access tokens live 15 minutes. Protected routes reject missing, malformed, and expired access tokens. Invalid credentials do not create a session. Credentials and raw tokens stay out of responses and logs.

nodes.label: Authentication Middleware
nodes.rationale: Middleware exposes the verified user identity to later handlers so each private route does not reimplement JWT checks.

nodes.label: Auth Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Registration, login, and refresh are rate limited so credential guessing and refresh storms are bounded before they reach password or token checks.

nodes.label: Refresh Token Rotation
nodes.rationale: Refresh tokens live 7 days, are stored as hashes, and rotate on use, returning a new access token. Sessions track owner, expiry, and revocation. Logout revokes the applicable session. Rotated or revoked refresh tokens cannot be reused successfully.

nodes.label: Registration
nodes.rationale: Registration stores a secure password hash. Duplicate normalized emails are rejected. Invalid requests use the agreed validation response. Database failures must not leave partial authentication records.

nodes.label: Token Family Revocation
nodes.rationale: Recommended baseline: reuse of a rotated token revokes its token family and requires reauthentication, so theft of an already-used refresh token cannot mint a sibling session.

nodes.label: Reset Account Privacy
nodes.rationale: Public reset responses do not reveal whether an email is registered, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts.

nodes.label: OTP Attempt and Resend Limits
nodes.rationale: Recommended defaults, pending approval: 10-minute expiry, at most 5 verification attempts, and a 60-second resend cooldown. Resend invalidates the previous OTP. Expired, incorrect, consumed, and invalidated OTPs are rejected. Rate limits apply by account and IP.

nodes.label: Password Reset Challenge
nodes.rationale: OTPs are stored in protected form, not plaintext, and are single-use. A successful reset consumes the challenge and stores the new password as a hash. Failures must not consume a challenge before the required work succeeds. Development console logging of OTPs must be off in production.

nodes.label: Reset Session Revocation
nodes.rationale: After a successful password reset, session handling follows the approved policy. The recommended behavior is to revoke existing sessions so a previously stolen refresh token dies with the old password.

nodes.label: Note CRUD
nodes.rationale: The owner can create and retrieve a valid note. Paths and payloads follow the approved API contract and are not invented in the ticket. Required search-data maintenance rides along with note writes so later search does not rebuild content from scratch.

nodes.label: Note Ownership
nodes.rationale: Every private note operation checks ownership. A user cannot access or modify another user's notes.

nodes.label: Soft Delete
nodes.rationale: deletedAt marks trash and removes the note from normal access. The owner can list and restore eligible trashed notes. The 30-day recovery window is preserved, and notes are not physically deleted during it.

nodes.label: TipTap Validation
nodes.rationale: Approved Decision 1: title max 200 Unicode code points after trim, whitespace-only titles rejected, canonical TipTap JSON, empty valid documents allowed, 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes, depth 20 with root at zero, 10,000 nodes, and only approved nodes, marks, attributes, and nesting. Shared schemas live in packages/shared. Backend validation is authoritative. Invalid or oversized content is rejected without persistence and is never silently truncated. Title limits count supplementary characters as code points.

nodes.label: Version Snapshot Transaction
nodes.rationale: The note and its initial snapshot either both persist or neither does. A qualifying update and its snapshot commit atomically. An unchanged update does not create a duplicate consecutive snapshot. A failed update leaves the note and its history unchanged.

nodes.label: AB-1006 Tag Model
nodes.rationale: Tag filtering uses the approved Tag and NoteTag model from AB-1006. Pagination and sorting can proceed without that schema, but tag filtering cannot be completed until AB-1006 supplies the association behavior. Ticket numbering does not override that dependency.

nodes.label: List Ownership and Trash Exclusion
nodes.rationale: Only the authenticated user's notes are returned, and trashed notes are excluded by default. Those filters run before pagination so page boundaries describe the caller's visible set.

nodes.label: Note Pagination
nodes.rationale: Recommended defaults, pending approval: page size 20, maximum 100. Omitted page size uses the default. Oversized page size follows the approved reject-or-normalize policy. Invalid pagination returns the agreed error. Ownership and deletion filters apply before pagination so other users' notes and trash never fill a page. Pagination can be built before tag filtering is finished.

nodes.label: Stable Note Ordering
nodes.rationale: Default order is updatedAt descending, then id as the tie-breaker. Only approved sort fields and directions are allowed. The tie-breaker exists so pagination does not duplicate or skip rows when timestamps collide.

nodes.label: Tag Filter
nodes.rationale: Recommended multi-tag semantics are AND: every selected tag must match. An empty tag filter returns the normal unfiltered list. Filtering and pagination work together. Completion waits on AB-1006's Tag and NoteTag association behavior. Queries should avoid N+1 access and add indexes from the real query shape. Shared Zod schemas stay synchronized with the API contract.

nodes.label: AB-1001 Project Setup
nodes.rationale: Highest-priority technical story to establish a reproducible monorepo so later features share one toolchain. Authentication, note logic, tags, search, sharing, version history, production cloud deployment, and full CI/CD are out of scope. No prior ticket dependency.

nodes.label: AB-1002 Authentication
nodes.rationale: Highest-priority story for registration, login, JWT access tokens, refresh rotation, and logout with database-backed sessions. Depends on AB-1001 and the approved authentication API contract and user/session schema. OTP reset, authentication UI, OAuth, admin roles, and note CRUD are out of scope. The API must match the approved OpenAPI contract.

nodes.label: AB-1003 OTP Password Reset
nodes.rationale: High-priority story for expiring single-use reset challenges and bounded verification attempts. Depends on AB-1001, AB-1002, and the approved password policy and reset API contract. Real email or SMS, frontend reset screens, support-assisted recovery, and login MFA are out of scope.

nodes.label: AB-1004 Note CRUD and Soft Delete
nodes.norm_label: ab-1004 note crud and soft delete
nodes.rationale: Highest-priority story for authenticated create, read, update, soft delete, trash listing, and restore, with strict content validation and transactional version snapshots. Depends on AB-1001, AB-1002, the Note and NoteVersion schema, the note API contract, and the content-validation policy. Editor UI, search, tags, sharing, history UI, and physical deletion during recovery are out of scope.

nodes.label: AB-1005 Pagination Sorting and Tag Filters
nodes.norm_label: ab-1005 pagination sorting and tag filters
nodes.rationale: High-priority story for a paginated, stably sorted note list with selected-tag filtering. Depends on AB-1001, AB-1002, AB-1004, and AB-1006 for the tag association contract. Tag CRUD, search, the notes-list UI, and unrelated CRUD changes are out of scope. Ticket numbering does not override dependencies.

nodes.label: Standard Error Shape
nodes.rationale: Every error is {error:{code,message,fields?}, requestId}. Clients never receive stack traces, secrets, or raw database errors. Structured diagnostics are logged with requestId.

nodes.label: Note-Taking App
nodes.rationale: Authenticated users create, organize, edit, search, share, and recover rich-text notes. Notes are single-user-owned. Real-time collaboration is out of scope.

nodes.label: Approved OpenAPI Contract
nodes.rationale: The approved OpenAPI contract is authoritative. The draft at openspec/changes/api-contract/delta-openapi.yaml is still x-proposed, and unresolved items stay in OPEN_DECISIONS.md.

nodes.label: packages/shared Contracts
nodes.rationale: The only place for cross-app Zod schemas, inferred types, validation constants, and error-shape types. Web and API import them rather than duplicating contracts.

nodes.label: Fixed Tech Stack
nodes.rationale: React 19, Vite, TanStack Query, Zustand, TipTap, and shadcn/ui on the web; Node 22, Express 5, PostgreSQL 16, and Prisma on the API; Vitest, Supertest, and Playwright for tests; pnpm workspaces. Do not substitute.

nodes.label: Express 5 API
nodes.rationale: Backend-only rules on top of root CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. Intended pnpm filter scripts exist, but package.json must be confirmed before they are run.

nodes.label: Local PostgreSQL 16
nodes.rationale: Compose service postgres uses image postgres:16, published only on 127.0.0.1:5432, with credentials from the environment and a pg_isready healthcheck. The tag is still floating until a patch pin is chosen.

nodes.label: React 19 Vite App
nodes.rationale: Function components and hooks only, one named export per file, shadcn/ui primitives first, and feature folders for notes, auth, and similar areas.

nodes.label: @notes/shared Contracts
nodes.rationale: The only place for types, schemas, and constants used by both backend and frontend. Status is empty and the layout is planned, so callers must check what actually exists.

nodes.label: GET /api/health
nodes.rationale: Returns 200 {status:ok} with no auth and no database call, so liveness does not depend on Postgres. Shared holds healthResponseSchema.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Derived from FRS and SDS for every AI tool on the team. If it conflicts with the FRS, SDS, or the approved OpenAPI contract, the spec wins and this file is fixed.

nodes.label: Engineer Agent
nodes.rationale: Implements one approved task with minimal scope and verifiable results, and stops if the work needs an unapproved design or specification change.

nodes.label: Reviewer Agent
nodes.rationale: Independent read-only review before merge. A PASS is a recommendation, not authorization to merge, and the reviewer must not modify source, tests, specs, or configuration.

nodes.label: Test Agent
nodes.rationale: Validates the app against approved specs and acceptance criteria. May change test files only. Must not modify application source, weaken assertions, or hide defects.

nodes.label: Implement Command
nodes.rationale: Reads AGENTS, FRS, SDS, domain CLAUDE, and the OpenSpec proposal, plan, and tasks before any code. Tests are written before or alongside implementation, and the change is archived when complete.

nodes.label: Plan Command
nodes.rationale: Produces a technical plan with file paths, TypeScript shapes matching SDS contracts, architecture reasoning, and backward-compatible DB notes, then waits for approval before implementation.

nodes.label: PR Command
nodes.rationale: Runs lint, test, and commitlint before drafting a conventional commit and a PR that cites FRS coverage, spec artifacts, and test coverage. Commit and push each require a yes.

nodes.label: Review Command
nodes.rationale: Read-only comparison of the implementation to spec scenarios and FRS criteria. Does not run graphify update. Output is compliance markers only, with no style feedback.

nodes.label: Spec Command
nodes.rationale: Creates an OpenSpec proposal from current specs, FRS, SDS, and AGENTS constraints after 3 to 8 clarifying questions, and does not proceed to implementation.

nodes.label: Start Command
nodes.rationale: Loads AGENTS, CLAUDE, FRS, SDS, domain CLAUDE files, and the graph report, then waits for a task instead of starting implementation.

nodes.label: Tasks Command
nodes.rationale: Breaks an approved plan into foundation, core, integration, and test phases, with a build, lint, and test checkpoint after each phase, and waits for approval.

nodes.label: AB-1001 Project Setup Session
nodes.rationale: Resume context for change ab-1001-project-setup. Phases 1-3 and 4a are done. Task 4.2 is blocked because the Docker daemon is not running. Nothing is committed.

nodes.label: Cross-User 404 Concealment
nodes.rationale: Cross-user access returns 404 rather than 403 so missing and forbidden resources look the same. This is proposed and still needs confirmation. Private endpoints verify the JWT and enforce ownership on the server.

nodes.label: Pinned Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Every dependency and tool version is pinned. @latest and floating ranges are forbidden, and the lockfile is committed.

nodes.label: Spec-Driven Test Layers
nodes.rationale: Vitest for unit tests, Supertest against a real PostgreSQL test database, and Playwright for end-to-end flows. Always cover ownership isolation, validation limits, transaction rollback, token reuse, and expired or revoked share links.

nodes.label: Central Error Handler
nodes.rationale: Routes throw typed app errors. One handler maps them to the AGENTS.md error shape and adds requestId. Express 5 forwards async rejections, so routes do not add try/catch wrappers.

nodes.label: Owner-Scoped Queries
nodes.rationale: Every private query puts ownerId = req.user.id in the where clause. Fetch-then-check is not enough, and userId or ownerId from the body or params is never trusted.

nodes.label: Graphify Before Code Exploration
nodes.rationale: Query Graphify before exploring source when the graph exists, then still read the relevant source and tests. After code changes, refresh with graphify update.

nodes.label: Compliance Findings Format
nodes.rationale: Findings are compliance-only: PASSED, MISSING, DRIFTED, SECURITY, and FRS GAP, each with severity, location, failure scenario, and a concrete fix. Style-only comments are out of scope.

nodes.label: Note-Taking E2E Scenarios
nodes.rationale: When the approved requirements include them, E2E covers register and login, note CRUD and reload, search and pagination, and ownership isolation. A scenario is not assumed to exist just because it is listed.

nodes.label: Acceptance Criteria Test Matrix
nodes.rationale: Every acceptance criterion maps to one or more tests covering happy paths, validation, auth and ownership, persistence, transactions, API errors, and UI states.

nodes.label: Session Context Management
nodes.rationale: Clear around 60k tokens after writing the task, decisions, and next step into notes or the OpenSpec change. One approved task per session, using the engineer, tester, and reviewer agents.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits
nodes.rationale: Imperative conventional commits, subject at most 72 characters, one logical change, and a requirement id in the body when relevant. Commit only when asked. Never commit directly to main.

nodes.label: One Task Per Branch
nodes.rationale: Branch names are type/short-kebab-description, optionally with a ticket id. One task per branch, and main is never committed to directly.

nodes.label: Ask Versus Proceed
nodes.rationale: Reads, in-scope edits, and lint, typecheck, unit tests, and builds proceed without a prompt. Contract changes, open decisions, dependency changes, Prisma migrations, and edits to FRS, SDS, or Claude settings wait for an explicit yes. Secrets, .env files, --no-verify, and force-push of main are never allowed.

nodes.label: Quality Gates
nodes.rationale: Stop at the first failure: pnpm lint including typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm build, then pnpm test:e2e only for user-flow changes and only with confirmation. Do not report done until the first three pass, and do not weaken a test or lint rule.

nodes.label: @notes/shared Public Entry
nodes.rationale: Apps import from @notes/shared only. src/index.ts is the only public entry point; deep paths are forbidden.

nodes.label: Pure Shared Package
nodes.rationale: No runtime dependency on React, Express, or Prisma, and no I/O, env access, or side effects, so the package works in Node and the browser. Changing a schema or constant is a contract change and needs an explicit ask.

nodes.label: Zod Schema Then z.infer
nodes.rationale: Define the Zod schema first and infer the TypeScript type. Do not hand-write a parallel interface or fork a close-but-wrong schema in an app.

nodes.label: pnpm allowBuilds
nodes.rationale: Native install scripts are allowed for @prisma/engines, esbuild, and prisma.

nodes.label: Backend Env Validation
nodes.rationale: Env validation lives in the backend with Zod and reports names only, not values. loadEnv() throws EnvError; server.ts prints name and reason lines and exits 1.

nodes.label: AB-1001 Version Pins
nodes.rationale: TypeScript stays on 6.0.3 because typescript-eslint's peer range is below 6.1.0. Prisma is 7.10.0 and Vitest is 5.0.4 because newer releases violate pnpm minimumReleaseAge; that policy is not relaxed.

nodes.label: OpenSpec change lifecycle (explore, propose, apply, sync, archive)
nodes.norm_label: openspec change lifecycle (explore, propose, apply, sync, archive)

nodes.label: Pinned Technology Stack
nodes.rationale: React 19, Vite, TanStack Query, Zustand, TipTap, and shadcn/ui; Node.js 22 and Express 5; PostgreSQL 16 and Prisma; JWT access tokens and database-backed refresh tokens; PostgreSQL full-text search; Vitest, Supertest, and Playwright; pnpm workspaces and packages/shared Zod types. Versions are pinned so builds stay reproducible, and floating @latest dependencies are forbidden.

nodes.label: Error Contract
nodes.rationale: Every error is {error:{code,message,fields?}, requestId}. fields is optional. Clients never receive stack traces, secrets, or raw database errors. Status codes run from 200, 201, and 204 through 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 413, 422, 429, and 500. 404 covers both unavailable and intentionally concealed resources.

nodes.label: OpenAPI Contract
nodes.rationale: Route paths, schemas, authentication requirements, and status codes come from the approved OpenAPI contract, delta-openapi.yaml during specification review. Implementation must not invent API behavior when the contract is silent.

nodes.label: packages/shared
nodes.rationale: Only packages/shared owns cross-application types, API contracts, and Zod schemas, so the web app and API cannot drift. Shared schemas include one deterministic serialization procedure for the content-size check. The HTTP body limit must fit a valid 1 MiB document plus a bounded envelope and still stay capped.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 16 is the source of truth. Indexes cover owner-scoped note listing, trash cleanup, tag filtering, token expiry, share-link lookup, and a full-text index over title plus readable TipTap text. Unique constraints cover normalized email, owner-scoped tag identity, and the note-tag pair.

nodes.label: Request Flow
nodes.rationale: React UI to API client to Express routes and middleware, then validation, application services, Prisma, and PostgreSQL. TanStack Query owns server state. Zustand holds transient client state. Business logic stays in application services so route handlers do not duplicate it. Public sharing uses a separate restricted read-only response path.

nodes.label: Environment Validation
nodes.rationale: Missing environment variables are reported safely, without committing secrets. An example environment file and setup docs cover prerequisites, environment, migrations, and commands.

nodes.label: Health Endpoint
nodes.rationale: A health endpoint returns the approved response and status so the scaffold can be checked before any business feature exists. It ships with tests.

nodes.label: pnpm Monorepo
nodes.rationale: pnpm workspaces split frontend, backend, and packages/shared. Node.js, pnpm, and dependencies are pinned, never @latest. TypeScript is strict. Root scripts cover build, lint, test, and development. Secrets stay out of source control.

nodes.label: Shared Package
nodes.rationale: Cross-app types and Zod schemas live only in packages/shared. Both applications must be able to import that package so contracts are not copied into each app.

nodes.label: Prisma PostgreSQL Configuration
nodes.rationale: Prisma is configured for PostgreSQL 16 and must connect to the configured database before later tickets add domain models.

nodes.label: Setup Quality Gates
nodes.rationale: Done means pnpm build, pnpm lint --max-warnings 0, and pnpm test pass, a sample automated test passes, and no secrets are committed. Vitest, Supertest, and Playwright are set up here even though product flows come later.

nodes.label: Functional Requirements Specification
nodes.rationale: Defines externally observable behavior, validation, security expectations, and acceptance criteria for single-user-owned notes. The SDS defines the implementation architecture.

nodes.label: Software Design Specification
nodes.rationale: Working draft and minimal implementation blueprint. The FRS defines functional behavior and OpenSpec holds approved change requirements. If implementation details conflict with approved requirements, stop and resolve the discrepancy before coding.

nodes.label: Local docker-compose Postgres 16
nodes.rationale: docker-compose.yml pins postgres 16 to a patch tag, uses a named volume, and takes local-dev credentials from .env only.

nodes.label: Prisma Datasource Without Models
nodes.rationale: schema.prisma has a generator and a PostgreSQL datasource only. Connectivity is SELECT 1, not a migration. Database tests are tagged so pnpm test passes without Postgres; test:db runs them against compose Postgres 16. prisma generate runs before typecheck.

nodes.label: Prisma With No Models
nodes.rationale: The datasource is postgresql via DATABASE_URL. db-check runs SELECT 1 and prints no credentials. No models and no migrations means there is nothing to roll back. Starting compose and running db-check needs approval at task 4.2.

nodes.label: Prisma Configured Without Migrations
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 16 is configured with a generator and datasource only, no models and no migrations, plus docker-compose, .env.example, and a SELECT 1 connectivity check.

nodes.label: Prisma Connectivity Tasks
nodes.rationale: schema.prisma is a generator and PostgreSQL datasource only, with no migrations. SELECT 1 and test:db need approval to touch the local compose database and must not print credentials when the host is unreachable.

nodes.label: pnpm Workspace Layout
nodes.rationale: frontend, backend, and packages/shared sit under a root pnpm workspace and a strict tsconfig.base.json with noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Turborepo and Nx were rejected as extra dependencies the spec does not call for.

nodes.label: Pinned pnpm Monorepo Scaffold
nodes.rationale: Adds a pnpm workspace with Node 22 and root scripts dev, build, lint, test, and test:e2e, plus a React 19 Vite frontend, an Express 5 backend, and a TypeScript plus Zod shared package. Dependencies are exact and need approval.

nodes.label: Fixed Tech Stack
nodes.rationale: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Query, Zustand, TipTap, and shadcn/ui; Node.js 22 and Express 5; PostgreSQL 16 and Prisma; a 15-minute JWT and a 7-day database-backed refresh token; PostgreSQL full-text search; Vitest, Supertest, and Playwright; pnpm workspaces; packages/shared with TypeScript and Zod. Versions are pinned.

nodes.label: Built Shared Package
nodes.rationale: packages/shared is compiled to dist with tsc and consumed as workspace:*. Project references and path aliases were rejected because Vite and Node resolve them differently. Dev runs tsc --watch so dist does not go stale.

nodes.label: D1 Layout Sign-off
nodes.rationale: The chosen layout is backend and frontend. SDS section 1 and AGENTS.md section 2 say apps/api and apps/web, and SDS allows a different approved structure. Editing SDS and AGENTS needs approval, then proposal, design, and tasks paths are renamed.

nodes.label: D2 Node 22 Engine
nodes.rationale: .nvmrc is 22, engines.node is at least 22 and below 23, and engine-strict is true. The scanned local Node 26 would fail install, so Node 22 is required before implementation.

nodes.label: Workspace Foundation Tasks
nodes.rationale: Root package.json, pnpm workspace, Node 22, save-exact, gitignore, strict tsconfig, ESLint flat config, and Prettier. The dependency list is approved before the first pnpm add. Lint is eslint with max-warnings 0 plus tsc --noEmit.

nodes.label: Exact Version Pinning
nodes.rationale: Node is pinned with .nvmrc and engines, pnpm with packageManager via Corepack, and dependencies are exact because .npmrc sets save-exact. The lockfile is committed only after the install-time list is approved.

nodes.label: D5 Install-Time Dependency Approval
nodes.rationale: Exact versions are resolved at install and listed for approval before pnpm add and before the lockfile is committed. The plan invents no version numbers.

nodes.label: AB-1001 OpenSpec Change
nodes.rationale: Spec-driven OpenSpec change created 2026-10-16 for project setup.

nodes.label: Spec-Driven Change Schema
nodes.rationale: The change schema is spec-driven, so implementation follows the approved OpenSpec artifacts.

nodes.label: Reviewer Then Archive
nodes.rationale: Run the reviewer agent against the diff and the AB-1001 acceptance criteria before the PR. Archive the change after review requirements are satisfied.

nodes.label: OpenSpec Workflow
nodes.rationale: Propose, approve, implement one approved task at a time, verify acceptance criteria, then archive. The engineer implements, the tester writes and runs tests, and the reviewer checks diffs. Branches are type/kebab-description. Conventional commits reference FRS ids. Never commit to main.

nodes.label: Vitest Supertest Playwright Scaffold
nodes.rationale: Vitest per package, Supertest for the API, and Playwright in the frontend with webServer wiring but only a skipped placeholder. test:e2e stays a separate script that needs confirmation. One sample unit test per package and one Supertest health test.

nodes.label: Web Scaffold Tasks
nodes.rationale: React 19 Vite frontend with a VITE_API_URL check, a shared import and Vitest test, and Playwright webServer wiring with a skipped placeholder listed by test:e2e --list.

nodes.label: DB-less Test Split
nodes.rationale: pnpm test is unit plus Supertest with no database. test:db runs tagged tests against compose Postgres. test:e2e only lists Playwright specs in this ticket. Health is mounted before future auth middleware and is excluded from later rate limiting by position.

nodes.label: Ordered Quality Checkpoints
nodes.rationale: Stop at the first failure: workspace install and lint, shared lint test build, API lint test build, prisma validate and an approved test:db, web lint test build and an e2e list, then root lint, test, and build with git status showing no .env.

nodes.label: Quality Gates and Required Coverage
nodes.rationale: Gate order is lint including typecheck, unit and integration tests, build, then e2e for user flows, stopping at the first failure. Supertest uses a real PostgreSQL test database. Required coverage includes ownership isolation, validation boundaries, transaction rollback, refresh-token reuse, expired or revoked share links, soft-delete consistency, and search that excludes deleted notes. Failed autosave keeps the local draft.

nodes.label: ESLint and Prettier
nodes.rationale: ESLint flat config with typescript-eslint plus Prettier. Root lint is eslint with max-warnings 0 plus tsc --noEmit per package. Biome was rejected by the user.

nodes.label: Prisma Domain Models
nodes.rationale: User, RefreshTokenSession, Note, Tag, NoteTag, NoteVersion, ShareLink, and PasswordResetChallenge. Schema changes go through Prisma migrations only. Final fields and indexes are confirmed in planning.

nodes.label: TanStack Query Server State
nodes.rationale: Notes, tags, search, versions, and shares live in TanStack Query with query-key factories and invalidation on mutation.

nodes.label: Zustand Client State
nodes.rationale: Zustand holds only transient UI such as the tag filter, sidebar, and editor draft status. Server data is never copied into Zustand.

nodes.label: Shared Content Module
nodes.rationale: Planned content folder holds the TipTap allowlist, content validator, canonical serializer, and text extractor.

nodes.label: Business Logic in Services
nodes.rationale: Business logic lives in application services, not in route handlers or React components.

nodes.label: JWT Access and Refresh Sessions
nodes.rationale: Login issues a 15-minute JWT and a 7-day refresh token stored hashed on RefreshTokenSession. Logout revokes the current session. Refresh-token transport, JSON body versus httpOnly cookie, is an open decision.

nodes.label: Note and Version Transactions
nodes.rationale: Create-plus-initial-version, update-plus-version, and version restore are transactional. Identical consecutive versions are deduplicated. Restoring a version creates a new version.

nodes.label: OTP Password Reset
nodes.rationale: OTPs are logged to the server console instead of emailed, so responses must not reveal whether an email is registered. Expiry is 10 minutes, attempts are capped at 5, resend cooldown is 60 seconds, and resend invalidates the previous OTP.

nodes.label: Auth and Search Rate Limits
nodes.rationale: Auth, OTP, refresh, search, and sensitive writes are rate limited per account and per IP.

nodes.label: Refresh Token Rotation
nodes.rationale: Refresh rotates the token. Reuse of a rotated token revokes the whole token family and forces re-login.

nodes.label: Request Flow
nodes.rationale: React UI to API client to Express routes and middleware, then validation, application services, Prisma, and PostgreSQL. TanStack Query owns server state; Zustand holds transient client state only.

nodes.label: Server-Authoritative Validation
nodes.rationale: Server validation is authoritative. Client validation is only fast feedback. Invalid input is rejected rather than silently truncated. API boundary types come from Zod via z.infer, not any.

nodes.label: Public Share Links
nodes.rationale: Tokens are random and unpredictable, default expiry is 7 days, maximum is 30 days, and non-expiring links are forbidden. The public path is read-only and must not expose version history, owner metadata, or editing. Views dedupe for 30 minutes per anonymous browser.

nodes.label: Thirty-Day Soft Delete
nodes.rationale: Soft delete sets deletedAt. Notes are never physically deleted within 30 days. An idempotent job then removes notes, versions, and share links past the recovery window.

nodes.label: TipTap Content Rules
nodes.rationale: Store canonical TipTap JSON, never arbitrary HTML, behind an allowlist. Title is at most 200 code points. Content is at most 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes, depth 20, and 10,000 nodes, checked with one deterministic serialization.

nodes.label: Idempotent Cleanup Job
nodes.rationale: The cleanup job must be idempotent and safe to run twice. Notes are not hard-deleted before the 30-day window.

nodes.label: Public Share Router
nodes.rationale: The public share route is a separate router with a narrow response DTO. It never reuses the owner note DTO.

nodes.label: Backend Request Layers
nodes.rationale: Routes, then auth and rate-limit middleware, then Zod validation from @notes/shared, then a service, then Prisma. Routes only parse, call one service, and shape the response.

nodes.label: Note Version Transactions
nodes.rationale: prisma.$transaction wraps create-plus-snapshot, update-plus-snapshot, and restore. Identical consecutive versions are deduped inside that same transaction.

nodes.label: Thinking Depth
nodes.rationale: Think hard for token rotation, ownership, transactions, validation limits, migrations, and anything touching the API contract. If the spec is silent or contradictory, stop and ask instead of inventing an answer.

nodes.label: In-Memory Access Token
nodes.rationale: The access token lives in memory, not localStorage. Refresh-token storage is an open decision, so the client must not pick a transport on its own.

nodes.label: Single API Client
nodes.rationale: All HTTP goes through one API client that attaches the access token and on 401 refreshes once and retries, otherwise logs out. Components must not call fetch or axios directly.

nodes.label: Debounced Autosave
nodes.rationale: Autosave is debounced and shows saving, saved, or failed. On failure the local draft is kept and retry is offered so unsaved content is never discarded.

nodes.label: TipTap Allowlist Match
nodes.rationale: Editor extensions must match the shared content allowlist exactly. Note content is rendered through the editor or a safe renderer, never dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

nodes.label: Prisma 7 pg Adapter
nodes.rationale: Prisma 7 needs @prisma/adapter-pg, pg, and prisma.config.ts. The prisma-client generator writes to backend/src/generated/prisma, which is gitignored and eslint-ignored and produced by the backend postinstall.

nodes.label: GET /api/health
nodes.rationale: Returns 200 with status ok, no auth, and no database call, and is mounted before later auth middleware. It is added to the draft OpenAPI as x-proposed. A database readiness probe was deferred because it needs a 503 the SDS status map does not contain.

nodes.label: service-health Capability
nodes.rationale: Unauthenticated liveness endpoint with a fixed response. GET /api/health returns 200 and status ok, needs no auth, and makes no database call. It is added to the draft OpenAPI as x-proposed pending approval.

nodes.label: Env Example and Gitignore
nodes.rationale: .env.example lists every required variable with a non-secret placeholder. Real .env files are ignored by git. Copying the example and starting local PostgreSQL 16 is enough to pass configuration validation.

nodes.label: Liveness Endpoint
nodes.rationale: GET /api/health responds 200 with JSON body status ok and a JSON content type while the process is serving requests.

nodes.label: API Config and Health Tasks
nodes.rationale: Express 5 createApp is separate from server.ts, with requestId, an SDS section 4 error handler, a safe 404 JSON body, parseEnv that never echoes values, GET /api/health without auth, shared imports, .env.example, and docker-compose Postgres 16.

nodes.label: Contract and Docs Tasks
nodes.rationale: Add GET /api/health to delta-openapi.yaml as x-proposed and a matching OPEN_DECISIONS entry, write setup docs, update AGENTS.md key commands, and finish with lint, test, build, and a git status that shows no .env.

nodes.label: Service Health Spec
nodes.rationale: Gives operators, developers, and tooling a cheap unauthenticated way to confirm the API process is up and serving requests.

nodes.label: Note Taking API Draft
nodes.rationale: OpenAPI 3.0.3 draft titled Note Taking API, version 0.1.0-draft, server url /api. Sources are FRS and SDS sections 4 and 5, which define no paths. Every route is x-proposed. Default security is bearerAuth. Open items are marked OPEN-n.

nodes.label: API Contract Open Decisions
nodes.rationale: Needed before delta-openapi.yaml can be approved. Nothing here is decided by FRS or SDS. Ruby YAML parsed 18 paths and 26 operations, all x-proposed, but the file is not verified against the OpenAPI 3.0.3 schema.

nodes.label: Note Taking Application
nodes.rationale: Project context sourced from FRS for what and SDS for how. If this file disagrees with them, FRS and SDS win. Day-to-day agent rules live in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: createApp Separated From Listen
nodes.rationale: createApp is separate from server.ts so Supertest imports the app without opening a port. A centralized error handler and requestId middleware use the SDS section 4 error shape and return no stack traces.

nodes.label: Backend parseEnv
nodes.rationale: The Zod env schema stays in the backend because env is not a cross-app contract. parseEnv returns a result or name-and-reason pairs. server.ts prints names and reasons and exits 1. Values are never included, and Zod messages map to a fixed reason set. The web app reads only VITE_API_URL.

nodes.label: createApp Without Env or Listen
nodes.rationale: createApp wires requestId, JSON parsing, routes, a 404, and the error handler, and it does not listen or read env. Tests never bind a port. The JSON body limit is deferred to AB-1004.

nodes.label: Central Error Handler
nodes.rationale: Unknown errors become 500 INTERNAL_ERROR. Diagnostics, including the stack, are logged with requestId and never sent to the client. Malformed JSON is 400 and oversize bodies are 413. A small structured console logger avoids a new logging dependency.

nodes.label: Pure parseEnv
nodes.rationale: parseEnv is pure. Zod issues map to missing when the value is undefined, otherwise invalid, so raw Zod text never reaches output. Required variables are NODE_ENV, PORT, and a postgres DATABASE_URL. A test asserts a sentinel secret never appears.

nodes.label: Open Decisions Left Unresolved
nodes.rationale: None of the 14 decisions in OPEN_DECISIONS.md is resolved. The health route is a new proposal added to that file for visibility. openspec/specs is empty, so no existing capability is modified.

nodes.label: Safe Configuration Error Reporting
nodes.rationale: Failure messages name the offending variable and the reason, missing or invalid, and must not print the variable value.

nodes.label: Startup Environment Validation
nodes.rationale: NODE_ENV, PORT, and DATABASE_URL are validated before requests are accepted. A missing or invalid variable exits non-zero and opens no HTTP listener. A non-numeric PORT is invalid. Valid values listen on PORT.

nodes.label: Database-Independent Health
nodes.rationale: The health endpoint does not query the database, so an unreachable PostgreSQL still returns 200 with status ok.

nodes.label: Public Minimal Health Response
nodes.rationale: The endpoint does not require authentication, including when no Authorization header is sent, and the body contains only status. It does not expose version, environment, configuration, or database details.

nodes.label: OPEN-0 Proposed Routes
nodes.rationale: FRS and SDS define no paths, methods, or field names. Every operation carries x-proposed true until approved or renamed. This is a plain draft because no spec command exists in the repo.

nodes.label: runtime-configuration Capability
nodes.rationale: Startup validation of required environment variables reports missing or invalid names and never leaks secret values.

nodes.label: Auth Register Login Refresh Logout
nodes.rationale: Public register returns 201 User or 409 on a duplicate normalized email. Login and refresh return AuthTokens in JSON. Reuse of a rotated refresh token revokes the token family and returns 401. Logout revokes the current refresh session and returns 204. Transport is OPEN-1.

nodes.label: Bearer JWT Access Token
nodes.rationale: HTTP bearer JWT with a 15-minute lifetime. Ownership is enforced server-side on every private resource, and another user's resource returns 404.

nodes.label: OTP Password Reset Flow
nodes.rationale: Request always returns 204 for a well-formed email whether or not it is registered, and the OTP is logged to the server console. Confirm takes email, otp, and newPassword, consumes the OTP, and returns 204, or 401 for an invalid, expired, or exhausted OTP. Both routes are rate limited, including a 60-second resend cooldown.

nodes.label: TipTap Document Schema
nodes.rationale: Canonical TipTap JSON with root type doc. The server validates approved nodes and marks, at most 1048576 UTF-8 bytes, depth at most 20, and at most 10000 nodes. The exact allowlist lives in packages/shared and is OPEN-13. Title is trimmed, non-blank, and at most 200 Unicode code points. Password is writeOnly and its policy is OPEN-12.

nodes.label: OPEN-8 OTP Confirmation
nodes.rationale: OTP format and length are unspecified. Invalid, expired, or exhausted OTP is drafted as 401, with 422 as the alternative. Confirmation is drafted as one step rather than verify-then-reset.

nodes.label: OPEN-12 Password Policy
nodes.rationale: FRS-AUTH-004 references an application password policy that neither FRS nor SDS defines.

nodes.label: OPEN-1 Refresh Token Transport
nodes.rationale: JSON body is drafted versus an httpOnly cookie for FRS-AUTH-002 and FRS-AUTH-003. The choice affects CSRF and the client. Proposed P9 puts tokens in JSON under /auth and remains undecided.

nodes.label: OPEN-13 TipTap Allowlist
nodes.rationale: The node, mark, and attribute allowlist must be fixed in packages/shared before validation can be specified. The OpenAPI schema stays intentionally loose until then.

nodes.label: Pre-Implementation State
nodes.rationale: Only specs, OpenSpec change drafts, and tooling exist. No apps, packages, or application code yet. Planned layout and commands are in AGENTS.md. Open decisions, including refresh transport and 404 versus an unused 403, must not be assumed.

nodes.label: AB-1001 Design
nodes.rationale: Pre-implementation design. The stack is fixed by SDS section 1 and AGENTS.md section 3. The draft API has no health route. Dependencies, Prisma migrations, and database work need approval. Gates run lint, then test, then build.

nodes.label: AB-1001 Technical Plan
nodes.rationale: Draft awaiting approval of D1 through D6. Inputs are the proposal, service-health and runtime-configuration specs, design, tasks, SDS sections 1 through 5, AGENTS.md, and the domain CLAUDE files. Implementation waits for a new instruction after opsx update.

nodes.label: AB-1001 Proposal
nodes.rationale: The repo holds only specs and tooling. AB-1001 is the foundation so later tickets have a reproducible pnpm monorepo and passing lint, test, and build. Nothing is breaking because there is no code yet.

nodes.label: Runtime Configuration Spec
nodes.rationale: The API refuses to start with missing or invalid configuration and reports the problem without leaking secret values.

nodes.label: AB-1001 Tasks
nodes.rationale: Workspace, shared package, and API scaffold tasks are done. Prisma connectivity, the web scaffold, root scripts, the contract update, and docs remain open. The reviewer runs before the PR, then the change is archived.

nodes.label: AB-1001 Out of Scope
nodes.rationale: Authentication, note logic, tags, search, sharing, versions, production deployment, full CI/CD, and JWT or auth env vars belong to later tickets, starting with AB-1002. Domain schemas and Playwright journeys are also out of this change.

nodes.label: P10 Ownership 404 Concealment
nodes.rationale: Proposed, not approved. Ownership failures return 404 and never 403 because SDS section 4 allows concealment and that avoids existence leaks. P1 through P12 are proposed; defined FRS and SDS behavior is carried over rather than newly decided.

nodes.label: OPEN-9 Registration Enumeration
nodes.rationale: FRS-AUTH-001 requires 409 for duplicate emails, while FRS-AUTH-004 says avoid revealing registered emails. A 409 on register leaks existence. Proposed P11 makes password-reset request always return 204.

nodes.label: TipTap Content Limits
nodes.rationale: Canonical content is TipTap JSON, never arbitrary HTML, behind an allowlist. Title is non-blank and at most 200 code points after trim. Content is at most 1048576 UTF-8 bytes, depth 20, and 10000 nodes. Empty valid documents are allowed. Backend validation is authoritative and never truncates. Body size is 1 MiB plus a bounded envelope.

nodes.label: Out of Scope Product
nodes.rationale: Real-time collaboration, attachments, native mobile, OAuth, nested folders, and real email delivery are out of scope. OTP is logged to the server console. Physical deletion during the recovery window is forbidden.

nodes.label: Security Requirements
nodes.rationale: Ownership is enforced server-side. Passwords and refresh tokens are hashed and never logged, nor are OTPs or share-token secrets. Refresh rotation with reuse detection revokes the token family. OTP lasts 10 minutes, allows 5 attempts, has a 60-second resend cooldown, and resend invalidates the previous OTP. Rate limits cover auth, OTP, refresh, search, and sensitive writes by account and IP. Share tokens are random, default 7 days, maximum 30, with no non-expiring links.

nodes.label: D3 HealthResponse and ErrorResponse
nodes.rationale: Shared ships ErrorResponse from SDS section 4 and HealthResponse so web and API prove the import path. fields items stay unknown arrays because OPEN-11 is unresolved. Both apps import only from @notes/shared, which depends on Zod and stays browser-safe.

nodes.label: Shared Health and Error Contracts
nodes.rationale: Both apps import HealthResponse and ErrorResponse from packages/shared as @notes/shared. No domain schemas yet. Strict TypeScript is enabled everywhere.

nodes.label: Draft Error Schema
nodes.rationale: Error requires error.code, error.message, and requestId, with optional fields of path and message. The code catalogue and item shape are OPEN-11. Shared responses cover 422 validation, 401 unauthorized, 404 not found or concealed, 409 conflict, 413 payload too large, and 429 rate limited.

nodes.label: Notes Resource
nodes.rationale: List own notes with page, pageSize, sort, order, and tagIds. Create writes the note and the initial version atomically. The owner can read trashed notes. Patch updates title or content in the same transaction as a snapshot and refuses edits of trashed notes. Delete sets deletedAt and is idempotent. Restore within 30 days is idempotent.

nodes.label: Page Pagination
nodes.rationale: page defaults to 1, pageSize defaults to 20 and maxes at 100, and list payloads include total. Invalid pagination is rejected with 422 under OPEN-5. Ids are drafted as UUIDs under OPEN-10.

nodes.label: Full-Text Search
nodes.rationale: GET /search queries the caller's non-deleted notes and returns a ranked page with highlighted snippets. Empty or punctuation-only queries and the highlight marker format are OPEN-7. The route is rate limited.

nodes.label: Share Links and Public View
nodes.rationale: One active share link per note. Create returns the token once; only a lookup or hash is stored. The owner can read status, expiry, and viewCount or revoke the link. Public GET /shared/{token} is unauthenticated and returns only title, content, and updatedAt. Expired, revoked, invalid, and deleted-note links all return the same 404. View counting is OPEN-2. expiresInDays is 1 to 30, default 7.

nodes.label: Tags Resource
nodes.rationale: List own tags with counts of non-deleted notes, create, rename, and delete a tag while keeping the notes. Assign or remove a tag on a note with idempotent PUT and DELETE. Name length and normalization are OPEN-14.

nodes.label: Note Versions
nodes.rationale: The owner lists versions newest first, inspects one version including its TipTap content, and restores it atomically. Restore is recorded as a new version. A snapshot that fails current validation returns 422.

nodes.label: OPEN-11 Error Code Catalogue
nodes.rationale: SDS gives only VALIDATION_ERROR and optional fields. The error code catalogue and the fields item shape are undecided. SDS lists 403, but ownership failures are drafted as 404 concealment, so 403 is unused until confirmed. Status 413 has no numeric cap beyond 1 MiB plus a bounded envelope, and rate-limit thresholds are unspecified.

nodes.label: OPEN-14 Tag Normalization
nodes.rationale: Case, maximum length, and the tag-count definition are open. The draft counts non-deleted notes only, following the FRS-TAG-001 text.

nodes.label: FRS Requirement Traceability
nodes.rationale: Every FRS requirement maps to at least one proposed operation, from register through version restore. Scheduled purge has no endpoint because it is a system job in SDS section 2.

nodes.label: OPEN-2 View Counting
nodes.rationale: Whether view counts happen inside GET /shared/{token} or a later client call is unspecified, as are anonymous-browser identity for 30-minute dedupe and bot exclusion.

nodes.label: API Error and List Conventions
nodes.rationale: JSON errors are error code, message, optional fields, and requestId. Statuses include 200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404 for missing or concealed, 409, 413, 422, 429, and 500. Lists default to page size 20, max 100, ordered by updatedAt descending then id. Tag filter is AND. The draft contract is still entirely x-proposed.

nodes.label: In-Scope Note Features
nodes.rationale: Authenticated users register, log in, log out, and reset passwords with OTP; create and autosave TipTap notes; soft-delete with 30-day recovery; paginate, sort, and filter by user-scoped tags; full-text search with highlights; public read-only share links; and per-save version history with restore.

nodes.label: User Visitor and System Roles
nodes.rationale: A registered user owns notes, tags, sessions, shares, and history. A public visitor views a valid share link only. The system validates tokens, rate-limits, expires links, and runs scheduled cleanup.

nodes.label: D6 Provisional Error Codes
nodes.rationale: Unknown routes return the SDS error shape with provisional code NOT_FOUND. Unknown errors map to 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with a generic message. Both strings are provisional because the code catalogue is OPEN-11.

nodes.label: List Sort Pagination and Trash Draft
nodes.norm_label: list sort pagination and trash draft
nodes.rationale: OPEN-4 drafts sort by updatedAt, createdAt, or title plus order. OPEN-5 rejects invalid pagination with 422. OPEN-6 disallows editing a trashed note while the owner may still read it. OPEN-10 drafts UUID ids and page plus pageSize and total. OPEN-7 leaves empty-query and highlight format open.

nodes.label: OPEN-3 One Share Link
nodes.rationale: FRS says a share link. The draft allows one active link and returns 409 if one exists. Expiry uses expiresInDays from 1 to 30, default 7. Proposed P8 keeps the owner share resource separate from the public token path.

nodes.label: Service and Persistence Constraints
nodes.rationale: Flow is UI to API client to Express middleware to validation to services to Prisma to PostgreSQL. Business logic stays in services. Only packages/shared owns cross-app contracts. PostgreSQL is the source of truth. TanStack Query owns server state and Zustand holds transient client state. Note create, update, and version restore are transactional. Soft delete uses deletedAt, and an idempotent job purges after 30 days. The approved OpenAPI contract is authoritative.

hyperedges.label: Engineer Tester and Reviewer Delivery Roles
